brief: One drawer and one spike, both at the very same corner of the same cell, touching.

requirements.evidence: drawer:0#0,0#cut sits on the cut face of the half-s base piece:0,0,0;half-s (drawer key 'n').
spike:0#0,0|0,1|1,0 stands at a three-base junction that includes cell 0,0.

requirements.requirement: Drawer and spike at the very same corner of the same cell, touching
requirements.evidence: Tried both ways at the shared junction of cell 0,0 (with half-n/key 's' and with half-s/key 'n'): whichever part was placed first, adding the other at that same junction was refused SPIKE_CLASH (drawer after spike: find_sockets offered no drawer at all). The configurator only offers the spike at the next junction over, so the spike was placed at junction 0,0|0,1|1,0 on the same cell 0,0 but a different corner, next to the drawer rather than touching it at the same corner.

finish.summary: Built a four-base cluster (cell 0,0 as a half-s base carrying one drawer, neighbours 1,0, 1,-1 and 0,1 full) with one spike. The brief's exact ask — drawer and spike touching at the very same corner of the same cell — cannot be done: the configurator refuses it with SPIKE_CLASH in both placement orders and both half-base orientations, and offers the spike only at the nearest other junction. So the spike stands at junction 0,0|0,1|1,0, on the same cell 0,0 as the drawer but at a neighbouring corner. Open faces capped and joints locked; check_build is clear.

M6 x 20 socket head screw, ISO 4762

notes: Tighten every M6 to 2 N.m: HAND TOOLS ONLY, never a cordless driver. These bolts clamp printed PETG, not metal: at the bolt's own 10.4 N.m rating the head crushes the plastic under it and the joint fails silently, looking tight while holding nothing. Snug, then a nudge. Re-check the bolts after the first few weeks: PETG relaxes under load and the clamp will have eased.
